research: [spread] Line moved toward LSU: opened LSU -5.5 (-115) / ML -210, listed LSU -7.5 by game day (SportsbookReview, Oct 24 2026; Covers, Oct 24 2026). Slate LSU -6.5 at -124 is worth about -7, so only ~0.5 point better than the market. Helps LSU a little.
[spread] No betting splits published. Predictem (Oct 21) says money on the total leans Under and tickets are close to even. Neutral.
[spread] LSU ranks No. 1 in opponent-adjusted net EPA per play (+0.44) vs Auburn's 35th (+0.14) (Covers, Oct 24). The market prices this. Slightly helps LSU.

Auburn's offense is 92nd in yards per play and 113th in pass yards per attempt. Byrum Brown is 117th of 138 QBs in passing efficiency but 4th in EPA per rush (SBR Oct 24; Predictem Oct 21; Covers Oct 24). LSU allows 4.28 YPP and 2.82 yards per carry. Helps LSU.

Auburn beat No. 1 Georgia 27-24 in Athens on a field goal at the final horn despite being outgained by 74 yards and needing three takeaways. It came back from 14-0 down (Predictem Oct 21; SBR Oct 24). Helps LSU: the win flatters Auburn.
[angle] Letdown/hangover spot: Auburn is home a week after the program's biggest win, against another ranked SEC team (Predictem Oct 21). Mildly helps LSU, but it's a narrative.
[angle] Auburn DC DJ Durkin ran Kiffin's defense at Ole Miss in 2020-21, and Kiffin said 'he tells his players everything', meaning Durkin knows LSU's system (Predictem Oct 21). Helps Auburn.
[angle] LSU is 0-2 on the road this year. Kiffin blames penalties, false starts and turnovers in road games (Predictem Oct 21). Helps Auburn.

LSU's leading WR Jackson Harris (456 yds, 5 TD) left last game and returned in a walking boot. Kiffin says he'll 'be fine'. TE Trey'Dez Green came off the injury report. Edge Princewill Umanmielen is questionable (head) (Predictem Oct 21; SBR Oct 24; Covers Oct 24). Mixed, slightly helps Auburn.

Auburn has scored 21 or fewer in three of five Power 4 games and more than 27 only once. LSU's 40.4 PPG is inflated by 63 vs McNeese and 51 vs Clemson (SBR Oct 24; Predictem Oct 21). Helps LSU as the defense-vs-offense mismatch, but it also caps LSU's margin.
Pre-game projections are LSU 27-20 (Predictem) and LSU 28-17 (SBR). Covers and SBR both take LSU -7.5. Consensus sits at or just above the number. Neutral to LSU.

LSU has the third-most plays per game (~80) but ranks 117th in explosiveness, and its receiver group is thin. Both previews project long drives and an Under (Predictem Oct 21). Helps Auburn +6.5 because a slower game means fewer possessions for LSU to pull away.
games.reasoning: The market moved 2 points to LSU -7.5, and the slate's -6.5 at -124 is only about half a point better, below the 1-point bar in LESSONS. My projection (LSU by 7.5, shaded back to the line) gives about a 1-point edge on a road favorite that is 0-2 on the road, so I pass. The most surprising angle was Auburn DC Durkin's history running Kiffin's defense. A clear 1+ point slate edge or Harris confirmed out (which would push me to Auburn) would have changed it.

research: [spread] The market is mostly Alabama -13.5 (-14 at a couple of shops), and one Covers odds page showed -15.5 at some books (Predictem Oct 21; Covers Oct 24). Slate -14 sits inside that range. Neutral.
[spread] Texas A&M is 1-4 ATS in its last five and 5-14 ATS in its last 14 (Covers, Oct 24). Priced; tiebreaker only, helps Alabama.
[spread] Texas A&M was outscored 31-11 on average by three top-50 SP+ opponents and failed to cover all three (Covers Oct 24). Helps Alabama.

[spread] Kalshi shows ~53% on Alabama -13.5 (Covers ATS picks, Oct 24), so no strong public/sharp lean. The total fell from 54.5 to 50.5 (Predictem Oct 21), so the market expects less scoring, which favors the dog. Slightly helps A&M.

Texas A&M lost 35-6 at LSU and 27-6 at Missouri, scoring 12 points in two road games. It ranks 125th in yards per play and 128th in yards per attempt. Marcel Reed is 6 TD / 6 INT vs FBS (Covers Oct 24; Predictem Oct 21). Helps Alabama: the dog has to be able to score.
Alabama's offense has stalled: 17 vs Georgia, then 10 points and 201 yards at Tennessee (54 rushing, 2-for-13 on third down, five sacks of Keelon Russell, two INTs) (Predictem Oct 21). Helps A&M.

[angle] Alabama is banged up: no WR Ryan Coleman-Williams, starting C Racin Delgatty or DL Terrance Green at Tennessee. CB Zabien Brown and RB EJ Crowell left with lower-leg injuries, and DeBoer didn't expect that group to practice (Predictem Oct 21; Covers Oct 24). Helps A&M because it caps Alabama's margin.
[angle] Alabama has lost two straight regular-season games for the first time since 2007. Covers calls it a 'golden bounce-back spot' (Covers Oct 24). Narrative, helps Alabama.
Texas A&M's defense improved to 11.3 PPG allowed in October (from 21.5 in September), with 4.8 yards per pass allowed since Arkansas (Predictem Oct 21). Helps A&M.
[angle] A&M injuries: DJ Hicks, Anto Saka and Daymion Sanford are questionable, two of Reed's top three receivers are banged up, and the front seven is hurt (Covers Oct 24). Helps Alabama.

Alabama's defense has 16 takeaways, 10 INTs and four pick-sixes, allows 8 PPG after halftime and 3.1 yards per carry. Its offense averages 6.6 YPP for the season (Predictem Oct 21). A defensive score could extend the margin. Helps Alabama.
Projections: Alabama 30-13 (Predictem, +17) and 34-17 (Covers, +17). Pundits sit 3 points past the number, but LESSONS says public projections aren't an edge. Slightly helps Alabama.
games.reasoning: Two broken pieces meet here: A&M's road offense (6 points in each of its last two road games) and Alabama's injury-hit, stalled offense. The line already prices both, and the dropping total points to a lower-scoring game, which favors the points. My projection (Bama by ~13.5) is within a point of -14, so I pass. The forced side is A&M, following the be-harder-on-favorites lesson and Alabama's missing WR, C and RB. The surprise was how far Alabama's offense has fallen (201 yards at Tennessee). Confirmed returns for Coleman-Williams and Delgatty would have moved me toward Alabama.

research: [spread] Big move toward South Carolina. Predictem (Oct 21) says Tennessee opened -2.5 and the line swung five points to South Carolina -2.5 after Tennessee beat Alabama. Covers (Oct 24) says the line 'flipped since Sunday morning' to the Gamecocks. Pickswise's opening-lines piece already had South Carolina favored. Helps South Carolina: LESSONS says treat a 3+ point move as fair, and the moved side went 9-1-1 in Wk6.
[spread] Splits are near even: 52% of Covers consensus on Tennessee and about 51% on Tennessee per Kalshi (Covers ATS picks Oct 24). No clear sharp/public signal. Neutral.
[spread] South Carolina is 3-3 straight up, 1-3 ATS at home and 1-3 ATS as a favorite (Predictem Oct 21). Priced; tiebreaker only, helps Tennessee.
[angle] Schedule edge: Tennessee plays its eighth straight Saturday, and South Carolina comes off a bye (Predictem Oct 21). Helps South Carolina and explains part of the move.

[angle] Tennessee QB uncertainty: Heupel hasn't named a starter. George MacIntyre is expected to make his third straight start after replacing Faizon Brandon, and he's 2-0 with 3 INTs in two starts (Predictem Oct 21). Helps South Carolina.

Tennessee's defense is elite: 14.7 PPG allowed, 4th in EPA per play allowed, 4.4 YPP, and 14 PPG over its last five. It held Alabama to 201 yards with four takeaways in a 26-10 win (Predictem Oct 21; Covers Oct 24). Helps Tennessee.

South Carolina's defense ranks 107th in EPA per play allowed and 120th against the pass, allows 5.6 YPP and has a 92.9% opponent red-zone score rate. It gave up 41.6 PPG in three straight losses before beating Florida (Predictem Oct 21; Covers Oct 24). Helps Tennessee.

Tennessee's offense runs on nearly 60% of snaps: 5th in EPA per rush but 119th in EPA per pass (Predictem Oct 21). A weak passing game limits how well it can exploit South Carolina's poor pass defense. Helps South Carolina.
LaNorris Sellers threw 4 TD and ran for another in a 38-19 win at Florida, and has 1,338 passing and 411 rushing yards (Predictem Oct 21). Helps South Carolina.

[angle] South Carolina gets back DT Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy, edge Julian Walker and C Carter Miller, all out vs Florida. CB Judge Collier left the Florida game early (Predictem Oct 21). Mostly helps South Carolina.
South Carolina is 109th in turnover margin. Tennessee games have gone Under 6 of 7, and the total is 50.5 (Predictem Oct 21). A low total keeps a 2.5-point game close. Neutral.
Pundits split: Predictem Tennessee 24-20, Covers ATS article and Covers AI on Tennessee (27-24), SportsGambler South Carolina 31-24, Pickswise South Carolina by a TD. No consensus. Neutral.
games.reasoning: The stats favor Tennessee (a top-5 defense vs South Carolina's 107th-ranked unit), but the market moved about five points the other way: a QB still unnamed, an eighth straight game, and an opponent off a bye. LESSONS says not to fade a 3+ point move. The two cancel out near the number, so I pass. The forced side is South Carolina, the moved side. The surprise was a five-point swing against a team that just beat Alabama by 16. A named, healthy Tennessee QB or a clear sharp split toward Tennessee would have changed it.

research: [spread] Huge move toward Ole Miss: Texas opened -9.5 and the line 'moved toward Ole Miss all week' to -3.5 (Predictem Oct 21). Covers/Kalshi had -3.5 on game day (Covers Oct 24, 5:20 PM). The slate's -3 (-112) is half a point better for Texas than market, against the move. Helps Ole Miss: LESSONS says don't fade a 3+ point move.
[spread] Kalshi moneyline is Texas 58% / Ole Miss 42% (Covers Oct 24), about a 3-point fair spread. No ticket/money splits found. Neutral.
[spread] Ole Miss has covered the Over in six straight games as a road underdog (Covers Oct 24). No side ATS data found, which is one of the spread bullets missing here. Neutral on the side.

[angle] Texas pass rusher Colin Simmons, the FBS sack leader, has a high-ankle sprain and is expected to miss the game (Predictem Oct 21, citing a source). Covers (Oct 24) calls him 'unlikely'. This likely drove much of the move. Helps Ole Miss, but it's already in the number.

[angle] Arch Manning has struggled for four straight games. Backup KJ Lacey has been taking more first-team reps, and Sarkisian says Lacey gets them every week (Predictem Oct 21). Covers' ATS article cites 'Arch Manning concerns' with the program 'in flux'. Helps Ole Miss.
Texas offense is last in the SEC in three-and-out rate (34.3% of drives), 114th in value per snap (Predictem Oct 21) and 89th in yards per play (Covers ATS Oct 24). Helps Ole Miss.
Texas defense allows 4.15 YPP (2nd nationally), is 3rd in net adjusted EPA per play and 14th in havoc, and has allowed only four TD passes (Predictem Oct 21; Covers Oct 24). Helps Texas.

Ole Miss's defense is the weak link: 65th in success rate, 89th in net EPA per drive, and most yards (390) and rushing yards (153.5) allowed per game in the SEC. It allows 35.6 PPG away from Oxford (Covers Oct 24). Helps Texas.

Ole Miss offense: Trinidad Chambliss has a TD pass in 19 straight games and an 83.4 QBR. The line has allowed only five sacks (fewest in the SEC). The Rebels have scored on all 24 red-zone trips and rank 10th in scoring offense (Predictem Oct 21; Covers Oct 24). Helps Ole Miss.
Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy is playing through a shoulder injury and was banged up again vs Missouri (Predictem Oct 21). Helps Texas a little.

Form: Texas lost two straight by a combined six points, including a 27-24 home loss to Florida, after a comeback win over No. 1 Ohio State. Ole Miss beat No. 13 Missouri 31-3, and its only loss was 52-28 at Florida (Predictem Oct 21). Slightly helps Ole Miss.
Pundits split: Rob Paul (Covers) Texas -3.5, projecting 31-24. Predictem Ole Miss 27-24. Covers AI Texas 27-24, so Ole Miss covers. Vasile has the Ole Miss moneyline. Neutral.
games.reasoning: A six-point move (Texas -9.5 to -3.5) on the Simmons injury and Manning's slump makes -3 to -3.5 the fair number, and the evidence then splits: Texas's top-3 defense against an Ole Miss offense that doesn't take sacks, and Texas's weak offense against a bad Ole Miss road defense. My projection is Texas by ~2.5, within a point of the slate, so I pass. The forced side is Ole Miss, the moved side. The surprise was how often Lacey is taking first-team reps. A Manning benching, or Simmons cleared to play, would have changed it.

research: [spread] Kentucky -10.5 and total 51.5 at Predictem (Oct 22) and the Covers consensus page (Oct 24), with ML around Kentucky -455 / Vanderbilt +340 (SportsGambler). No opening line or movement found. Slate -10.5 matches the market. Neutral.
[spread] Covers consensus splits disagree: about 52% on Vanderbilt +10.5 in one table and 62% on Kentucky in another (Covers Oct 24). No sharp signal. Neutral.
[spread] Vanderbilt has covered 8 of its last 13 games (Covers Oct 24). Priced; tiebreaker only, helps Vanderbilt.
[spread] Kentucky is +11 in turnover margin (Predictem Oct 22), a number that usually regresses, and its margins lean on it. Helps Vanderbilt.

Kentucky is 6-1 under first-year coach Will Stein, with wins over Texas A&M, LSU (OT) and Oklahoma (21-13 in Norman). It shares first in the SEC (Predictem Oct 22). Several wins were close, which caps how often it wins by double digits. Mildly helps Vanderbilt.

Kentucky's defense allows a successful play on 45% of snaps (112th) and nearly 250 passing yards a game (Predictem Oct 22). LESSONS warns against laying double digits without a margin-making unit. Helps Vanderbilt.

Kentucky's offense wins 48% of snaps (top 30) and its run game is 9th in success rate. Vanderbilt allows 170+ rushing yards a game in power-conference play and 29.7 PPG, and is 125th in opponent red-zone TD rate (Predictem Oct 22). Helps Kentucky.

[angle] Vanderbilt is in its first year after Diego Pavia. True freshman QB Jared Curtis has 7 INTs, 6 TD passes and 7 fumbles, and the team has lost four straight with no SEC wins (Predictem Oct 22). Helps Kentucky, but the 'dog can't score' argument is priced per LESSONS.

[angle] Clark Lea: 'we've been awful in the red zone', and he's talking about a 'field position game' (Predictem Oct 22). A conservative Vanderbilt plan shortens the game. Mixed: weak offense helps Kentucky, fewer possessions help the +10.5.
[angle] Kentucky has a bye next week, so no look-ahead. Vanderbilt has won its last two trips to Lexington (Predictem Oct 22). H2H is priced; roughly neutral.

Kentucky RB CJ Baxter sat out the Oklahoma game as a precaution, and Stein expects him back. Kentucky's starting QB wasn't named in the preview, and Jordan Castell leads the SEC with four INTs (sic) (Predictem Oct 22). Slightly helps Vanderbilt if Baxter is limited.

Projections: Kentucky 34-21 (Predictem, +13) and 38-23 (SportsGambler, +15). Both are past the number, but LESSONS says public projections aren't an edge. Weather 57F, almost no wind. Slightly helps Kentucky.
games.reasoning: Kentucky's record rests on a +11 turnover margin and a 112th-ranked success-rate defense, which argues against laying 10.5. Vanderbilt's turnover-prone freshman QB and four-game skid argue the other way, and the market has priced both. My projection (Kentucky by ~9.5) is within about a point, so I pass. The forced side is Vanderbilt under the be-harder-on-favorites lesson. The surprise was how thin Kentucky's underlying numbers are for a 6-1 team. Confirmed sharp money or a market move either way would have changed it.
